description.value: The Sncewips Heritage Museum is an Indigenous-owned and operated institution of the Westbank First Nation, dedicated to preserving and sharing sqilxʷ (syilx) culture, language, and heritage. Founded as a repository in 2005 and opened to the public in 2014, it offers self-guided drop-in visits by donation as well as bookable guided tours covering self-government, traditional tools, storytelling, and more. It has won multiple Kelowna Chamber of Commerce Business Excellence Awards and is a recognized cultural destination in the Okanagan.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content is fully accessible and confirms the museum is open and operating at Unit 260, 525 Highway 97, Kelowna BC V1Z 4C9, with phone (778) 755 2787 and email museum@wfn.ca. The website makes no mention of bike parking, washrooms, water refill, or any cyclist-specific amenities, so those fields default to null. The museum is an Indigenous-owned heritage attraction operated by Westbank First Nation, publicly accessible by donation or guided tour booking.
concerns: OSM record has no osm_id, address, or phone tags — all contact details sourced from website only. Phone formatted as (778) 755 2787 on website; OSM field was empty so contact_confirmed.phone set to null.
No OSM geometry or ID provided; coordinates appear to place the museum at Highway 97 in West Kelowna, which is consistent with the listed address.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A real, publicly accessible, award-winning Indigenous heritage museum in Kelowna, open to drop-in visitors by donation — a worthwhile stop for any touring cyclist exploring the Okanagan.
enrichment_extras.notes: Entry is by donation for self-guided visits; guided tours require pre-booking. The museum notes it is a non-profit society relying on donations.
